gen-dafont-true-north-satoshi: Stocky, tall-waisted capitals with curves that won't quite close. Satoshi takes the opposite tack, a soaring x-height and an open e, with every stroke the same width, so True North gets the swagger and the sans gets the talking.
gen-dafont-true-north-switzer: True North squats on a tall middle band, its curves left ajar, while Switzer's wire-like sans strokes keep their visual mass uniform from letter to letter. Give the body a modest size.
gen-dafont-true-north-work-sans: Curves left deliberately ajar, packed into a stocky line.
gen-dafont-visitor-bitter: Visitor looks soldered from bent wire, with gaping e mouths and short ascenders over big round bowls. Bitter, a slab-serif, does the steadier work.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-epunda-slab: Visitor feels like a glowing old terminal.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-fauna-one: Short ascenders perched over big bowls give Visitor a pixel-era look, like solder pulled through a nozzle. Fauna One, a text serif, handles the actual reading.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-glegoo: Strokes pulled like solder through a nozzle give Visitor its nostalgic, digital look, never mixing bold and light in a word. And Glegoo, a classic serif, opens its big counters in a tall lowercase, so long reading feels refined and unhurried.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-hanuman: Hanuman is a text serif with a high-waisted lowercase and wide-set terminals on its s. And over a longer stretch it reads traditional and refined, a quiet counterweight to Visitor's wire-bent display letters.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-kadwa: Kadwa, a text serif, runs on open-ended curves and an unusually large x-height, so it reads with an editorial ease. A slightly larger body size would suit it.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noticia-text: Visitor's gaping e mouths and strokes pulled like solder give it a nostalgic, digital stare. Noticia Text, a text serif, answers with big entrances into every curve.
